help.howitworks.switching_service_source.backTranslation: Progress: If choosing a source would discard progress already made, DebridPulse first asks Discard downloaded progress?. A service switch that would discard progress is instead rejected, with the reason would discard downloaded data; to confirm, switch the link's source.

While a download is paused: Choosing a different source for a file whose download had already begun is accepted and saved, but nothing starts. The displayed service and displayed source remain the current ones, and next to the service name a message names where the file will switch to, for example Switching to Real-Debrid (rapidgator.net) on resume. Choosing again replaces it; choosing the source already in use removes it. After resuming it reads Switching to … until the switch takes effect, and then disappears. If a download's paused files would switch to different destinations, or the destination is unknown, no destination is shown. A file that never started has nothing to hand over; its new source therefore simply applies as soon as it starts. Choosing a service during the pause works as described above, except that the download stays paused: a service that can take over the link in use takes over immediately (the badge shows it), and one that must first prepare a copy shows Preparing at … and only takes over after resuming. These messages appear in the rows of Download Activity and of Downloads; both kinds can appear at the same time.

help.howitworks.backup_torrents.each_deb.backTranslation: Each debrid service has a Prepare backup torrents switch. It is on by default for AllDebrid, Debrid-Link, Premiumize and Real-Debrid and off by default for TorBox, whose torrent limits are tighter. While it is on, that service also adds torrents that another service is currently delivering, so that it can take over if needed; and when you switch a download to another service, the torrent already started is kept as a backup instead of being removed. This occupies that account's torrent slots and limits; a new download that needs a slot takes it back first. Turn it off to keep this service's slots free for its own downloads: its backups are then removed. A choice already saved is kept.

help.settings.users_access.user_accounts.backTranslation: User Accounts lists each person with their role, with the way they sign in and whether the account is enabled. Add local account creates an account with a username and password. A role changed in Edit user applies immediately: that person's open pages reload with the new role without signing them out. Each person has a DebridPulse username that is separate from their display name: an OIDC account takes it over at its first sign-in, and the person signs in with this name for password sign-in; the pencil next to it in the Edit user title changes it and keeps a saved password. Click an account's name to see its details and its activity; there an open request can be withdrawn individually. Disable and Remove first show how many open download requests the account has; these requests are withdrawn, a transfer that someone else also requested keeps running, and completed downloads are never touched. Disabling also ends the account's sign-ins and revokes its tokens; removing keeps the account's history and deletes its own notification settings. If a removed OIDC sign-in returns, it gets a new account that stays disabled until you enable it. Merge combines two or more accounts into the account you want to keep; two accounts with the same verified email address are pointed out, but only a merge combines them. DebridPulse always keeps at least one usable Admin, and you can neither change your own role nor disable your own account.
